intro: Word for journalists on Mac is a practical tool for drafting, tracking editor changes, and filing copy. It works well when you rely on four basics: Track Changes, comments, Read Aloud, and templates. This page covers those basics, the version checks that matter in 2026, and where Lazur helps by voice.
tldr: Check your macOS and Word versions first. Microsoft says macOS 14 or later is required to keep receiving Office updates.
Office 2021 for Mac reached end of support on October 13, 2026. Move to a supported version before a busy filing week.
Use Track Changes and comments for editor edits. Press ⌃⌥Space to hear your copy with Read Aloud.
Save recurring stories as .dotx templates, and know where your template folder lives.
Lazur sees your screen while you hold ⌥⌘, points at controls, and drafts or dictates text. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: How reporters use Word for Mac on a normal day

Most reporting work in Word on a Mac runs in the same loop. You draft, an editor marks up the copy, and you fix it before it goes to the content system. Each step asks something different from the app. The draft needs space to think. The edits need Track Changes. The final copy needs a clean read.

That is why the basic tools matter more than the fancy ones. Learn four things first: Track Changes, comments, Read Aloud, and templates. Those four cover most of a reporter's week in Word. The rest of this page goes through them in the order you will need them on deadline.
Check your macOS and Word versions before deadline week

Start with the two checks that decide whether Word keeps getting fixes. The first is macOS. Microsoft says a minimum of macOS 14 (Sonoma) is required to receive updates to Microsoft 365 and Office apps. If you stay on an older macOS, Word still opens. You stop getting updates, including security updates.

The second is the Office version. Office 2021 for Mac reaches end of support on October 13, 2026. That date has passed. An Office 2021 install gets no more security updates. Microsoft supports Office on the three most recent major versions of macOS, so check that list before you update your Mac.

Then check the build. Microsoft's release notes list Word for Mac version 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026. The only Word item in that entry is quality and performance improvements. To find your build, open Word and choose Word > About Word. Compare the number you see with the one in the release notes.
The reduced functionality warning

Microsoft's known-issues page warns about something worse than a slow update. Starting July 13, 2026, some Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS may enter reduced functionality mode. So may users of non-subscription Office 2021 or 2019. In that mode, apps can open and print files. They cannot edit, save, or create new files.

For a reporter, that is a filing emergency. Check your subscription status and your install type now, not when your editor is waiting. Microsoft's page was last updated in July 2026, so read its current status before you rely on it.
Track Changes and editor comments without losing your place

Editors usually send edits back as tracked changes or comments. In Word for Mac, the work lives on the Review tab. Turn on Track Changes before you accept any edit. Then the desk can see what changed and who changed it.
Here is a routine that holds up on a busy day:

items: Turn on Track Changes before you start your own edits.
Reply to each comment in the margin, even with one word like 'Done' or 'Checked'.
Accept or reject edits one paragraph at a time, not all at once.
Before you file, check that no tracked change is left that the desk did not ask for.

blocks.text: Two mistakes show up again and again. The first is accepting every change in one click, which can hide a fact fix you still need to check. The second is deleting a comment thread after you act on it. Resolve the thread instead. The editor keeps the context, and you keep the record.
Compare two drafts without a grayed-out file

Microsoft's known-issues page lists 'Files are grayed out when using the compare feature', with a workaround. If the file looks grayed out during a compare, read the workaround on that page first. Save a named copy before you compare, so the older draft stays safe.
Hold ⌥⌘ and ask, 'Lazur, where is Track Changes?' Lazur circles the control on your screen and labels it. It does not click the control for you. You do that, so you stay in charge of every change.
Use Read Aloud to catch errors your eyes skip

Read Aloud is the cheapest proofreading tool you already own. It reads your copy out loud, so missing words, doubled names, and run-on sentences stand out. Start it from the Review tab, or press ⌃⌥Space. Press ⌥Space to play or pause. Press ⌥↑ or ⌥↓ to skip paragraphs.

Microsoft lists Read Aloud as a subscriber feature. It is available in Microsoft 365, Office 2021, and Office 2019. Open the gear icon to change the reading speed and voice. Pick a voice you can stand to hear for the length of a full story.

Read Aloud has limits. A quote with a missing 'not' sounds wrong, and you hear it right away. A wrong figure that sounds normal slips past. Check every number against the source, line by line. Read Aloud helps with rhythm and missing words. It will not confirm that a quote is accurate.
A good routine is two passes. Listen once for facts, names, and attribution. Listen again for rhythm and sentences that run on. Two short passes beat one long, distracted pass.
Save templates for the stories you write every week

Recurring stories need the same frame each time. A council meeting brief, a corrections note, and a profile intro all have standard parts. Build one clean document with the headings and boilerplate. Then save it as a template, so you start from the frame and not from a blank page.

items: Open the finished skeleton document in Word.
Pick Microsoft Word template (.dotx) for plain text and headings.
Pick Microsoft Word Macro-Enabled template (.dotm) only if the file contains macros.
Give it a clear name, such as Council brief template, and save.
Open new stories from the template, so the original stays clean.

blocks.text: By default, Word for Mac saves user templates to /Users/<username>/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/User Content/Templates. Replace <username> with your Mac account name. You can move the folder. Choose Word > Preferences > Personal Settings > File Locations, select User templates, and choose Modify.

A corrections template is a good first build. Keep four fields: the original text, the corrected text, the date, and the editor who approved it. One screen covers all four. Everyone on the desk fills it in the same way, so nothing gets lost.
Template mistakes that leak into copy

The most common mistake is saving a template with real quotes, names, or figures still in it. The next reporter sees them. Clear every real detail before you save. Keep placeholders in square brackets, so nobody mistakes them for final copy.
Dictation and drafting in Word on Mac

Typing is slow when you have a voice memo open and a notebook beside you. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor. Dictation works in any app, Word included. Add names and place names to your personal dictionary first, so they come out right.

What do journalists actually use AI for? The Reuters Institute surveyed 1,004 UK journalists between August and November 2024. Their most frequent uses, at least monthly, were transcription or captioning, translation, and grammar checking or copy-editing. The chart shows the figures.

Two cautions apply. The survey covers AI tools in general, not Word. It also covers UK journalists only. The same survey found that frequent AI users were more likely to say they work too often on low-level tasks. Use AI for the chores, then spend the saved time on reporting and on the sentences that need a human eye.
Research and sourcing without losing the thread

Microsoft 365 for Journalists lists Word resources, including research directly within Word and OneNote. That is Microsoft's own tool. Check which research features your Microsoft 365 plan includes before you build a process around them. Microsoft describes the program as free for enterprise license customers.

Lazur research works differently. It runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, using the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Use it to find candidate sources, then open each one yourself.

The mistake to avoid is pasting a summary into copy without checking the source. Summaries flatten qualifiers. A source that says 'may' can read as 'will'. Go back to the original sentence before you quote it, and note the page in your draft.
Keep the file safe on deadline

Microsoft's known-issues page lists two open items that matter at filing time. Some users on macOS report problems printing from Word. Others get prompted to save locally saved documents after being idle with no edits made. Both are marked as under investigation, and the page was last updated in July 2026.

Build habits that cover both problems. Save a named copy before each big edit with File > Save As. Keep the story in a folder your desk can reach. If you need a press check, print a PDF first and open that PDF to test it.
When a save prompt appears after a pause, read it before you click. Do not assume Word saved your last paragraph. Check the title bar for the file name, then save.
Common mistakes journalists make in Word on Mac

items: Staying on Office 2021 after October 13, 2026, when Microsoft ended support.
Filing with Track Changes still on, so the desk sees every deletion.
Saving templates to a folder you never open again.
Treating one Read Aloud pass as a full edit.
Letting an AI summary stand in for the original source.
Assuming the reduced functionality warning is gone without checking Microsoft's page.

blocks.text: Each mistake costs time at the worst moment. Fix them on a quiet afternoon, not during filing.
What Lazur does and does not do inside Word

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on your screen, and Lazur answers out loud. In Word, that means it can see the page, point at the control you need, and explain what it shows.

Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. It does not click buttons, edit files, or operate Word for you. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Word or any other app.

Lazur also drafts and types text. Hold fn to dictate at the cursor. Ask for a draft, and the text lands where your cursor sits. Then you read it, cut it, and decide what stays. See [Word for Mac with Lazur](/apps/word) for what Lazur sees, points at, and dictates in Word.

Privacy works like this. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
A worked example: drafting a standfirst from council notes

Say you have raw council notes and a deadline. Your editor wants a standfirst, the short line under the headline. Select the notes in Word. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask Lazur for a two-sentence standfirst from the selected notes. Lazur types the draft at the cursor.

Now you edit. Press ⌃⌥Space and listen to the draft. Cut any line that sounds like a press release. Check every figure against the notes. Good standfirsts give the reader the fact and the stake. Weak ones repeat the headline in other words.
This is where Lazur saves the most time. The draft is a starting point, not copy. You still own the claim, the figure, and the choice of words.
Pricing, platforms, and where to start

Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available. Lazur has a Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Check [current plans on the pricing page](/pricing) before you decide.

Start with the Word habits on this page. Then try one task on a real story. Good first tests are a Read Aloud pass, a template save, or a standfirst draft. [Download Lazur](/download) and run one of them. If your desk works in Google Docs, read [Google Docs for journalists on Mac](/for/journalists/google-docs) as well.

faq.question: Is Word for Mac still supported on Office 2021?
faq.answer: Not for security. Microsoft says Office 2021 for Mac reached end of support on October 13, 2026. That date has passed, so that install gets no more security updates. Check Microsoft's lifecycle page, then move to a supported version before your next filing week.

faq.question: Where does Word for Mac save my templates?
faq.answer: By default, user templates go to /Users/<username>/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/User Content/Templates. To change the location, open Word > Preferences > Personal Settings > File Locations, choose User templates, then select Modify.

faq.question: Does Read Aloud work in Word for Mac without a subscription?
faq.answer: Microsoft lists Read Aloud as a subscriber feature in Microsoft 365, Office 2021, and Office 2019. Check the Review tab on your install. If the option is missing, check your plan on Microsoft's support pages.

faq.question: How does Lazur work alongside Word on my Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur lives in the notch on your Mac, next to Word. It is not a plugin or add-in for Word or any other app. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold ⌥⌘, and it answers out loud.

faq.question: Will Lazur click buttons or edit my document?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points, circles, and guides you one click at a time. When you ask, it drafts and types text at your cursor. It does not click buttons or edit files for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur store what I say about my story?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Why does Word ask me to save after I stop typing?
faq.answer: Microsoft's known-issues page lists a prompt to save locally saved documents after being idle with no edits made. Microsoft marks it as under investigation. Save a named copy, and read the prompt before you click.

faq.question: Can Lazur check the facts in my story?
faq.answer: Lazur can run research in its own Chrome tabs and return a summary and a report. Treat that as a list of leads. Open every source, and check the exact wording before you quote it.

faq.question: What if Word will not save or edit my file?
faq.answer: Microsoft's known-issues page warns that from July 13, 2026, some Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS, and non-subscription Office 2021 or 2019 users, may be in reduced functionality mode. In that mode, apps can open and print but not edit, save, or create files. Check your plan and install type on that page.
